item.dc:creator: newsroom

The event will feature work from more than 200 artists, with booths showcasing everything from paintings and sculptures to crafts and mixed media. item.content:encoded:
Downtown Pensacola's fall art tradition kicks off this weekend as the 54th annual Great Gulfcoast Arts Festival takes over Seville Square. The event will feature work from more than 200 artists, with booths showcasing everything from paintings and sculptures to crafts and mixed media.

According to InWeekly, the festival draws art enthusiasts and creators alike to the historic square, where live oak trees provide shade and a stage for live music throughout the weekend. The event has become a signature fall gathering for the Pensacola community, blending art sales with entertainment and the chance to meet local and regional artists.

The Great Gulfcoast Arts Festival is free to attend and open to the public. It's an opportunity for artists to connect directly with buyers and for visitors to discover original work and support the creative community.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Animal Services launches holiday foster program
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Animal Services is offering pet lovers a chance to foster animals over the upcoming holidays through its "Home for the Pawlidays" program, providing temporary homes for shelter pets during Thanksgiving and Christmas. The program runs in two sessions: November 18 through December 3 for Thanksgiving, and December 14 through January…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Animal Services is offering pet lovers a chance to foster animals over the upcoming holidays through its "Home for the Pawlidays" program, providing temporary homes for shelter pets during Thanksgiving and Christmas.

The program runs in two sessions: November 18 through December 3 for Thanksgiving, and December 14 through January 4 for Christmas. Interested foster parents can complete an application, and staff will match them with a pet based on the home environment and animal needs. All pets currently available for adoption online are eligible for fostering.

The shelter covers all foster expenses, including food, toys, treats, harnesses, and leashes. Foster families are encouraged to share photos, videos, and behavioral observations with staff — insights that help the shelter better understand each animal and prepare potential adopters. Those who decide to permanently adopt their foster pet will have adoption fees waived.

According to Santa Rosa County, the program gives shelter animals a break from institutional life and temporarily reduces the number of pets in care during the busy holiday season. Interested residents can call the shelter at 850-983-4680 for more information or to schedule a time to meet animals before fostering.

item.title: City of Pensacola Cancels Title Search RFP Oral Presentations, Reschedules SAFE Pensacola Committee Meeting
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Pensacola has made scheduling adjustments to two procurement processes underway for federal grant-funded programs. The selection committee for RFP 26-064, which seeks pre-qualified title search services providers for Community Development Block Grant and other housing programs, will not hold its originally scheduled oral presentations…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola has made scheduling adjustments to two procurement processes underway for federal grant-funded programs.

The selection committee for RFP 26-064, which seeks pre-qualified title search services providers for Community Development Block Grant and other housing programs, will not hold its originally scheduled oral presentations on December 8, 2026. The city announced that a recommendation of award has already been made by the committee at an earlier shortlist meeting, making the presentations unnecessary.

Meanwhile, the selection committee for RFQ 26-066—the Streets Are For Everyone (SAFE) Pensacola initiative—has rescheduled its material distribution and guidelines review meeting from November 6 to November 13, 2026, at 10 a.m. The public meeting will be held at City Hall, Whibbs Conference Room, 222 W. Main St. The city has not specified reasons for the one-week delay.

item.title: Ruth's List Florida celebrates 27 Democratic women wins statewide
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Ruth's List Florida, an organization dedicated to electing Democratic pro-choice women to office, is celebrating a successful election cycle following Tuesday's vote, with 27 endorsed candidates winning races across the state — a 75 percent win rate. Among the headline victories was Tiffany Moore Russell's election as Orange County Mayor, making…
item.content:encoded:
Ruth's List Florida, an organization dedicated to electing Democratic pro-choice women to office, is celebrating a successful election cycle following Tuesday's vote, with 27 endorsed candidates winning races across the state — a 75 percent win rate.

Among the headline victories was Tiffany Moore Russell's election as Orange County Mayor, making her the first Black woman to hold that office. The organization also secured legislative gains in the Florida House and Senate, including House District 106 where Lucia Báez-Geller flipped a seat that had been held by Republicans. Several county commission seats changed hands in victories attributed to Ruth's List endorsements, including wins in Hillsborough, Palm Beach, and Orange counties.

"These victories are a testament to the extraordinary women who stepped up, ran tough campaigns and earned the trust of voters across Florida," said Christina Diamond, CEO of Ruth's List Florida. The organization provided campaign training, fundraising support, and on-the-ground assistance to candidates throughout the election cycle, according to a news release issued Wednesday.

The results represent gains for Democrats in state legislative races and in traditionally Republican strongholds in Central Florida and Miami-Dade County, the organization said.

item.title: USPS Operation Santa opens adoption registration for holiday gift-giving
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service has opened registration for Operation Santa, its annual program connecting people in need with donors willing to fulfill their holiday wishes. Northern Florida residents and organizations can now sign up to adopt letters at USPSOperationSanta.com, according to a USPS announcement Wednesday. Prospective adopters must…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service has opened registration for Operation Santa, its annual program connecting people in need with donors willing to fulfill their holiday wishes. Northern Florida residents and organizations can now sign up to adopt letters at USPSOperationSanta.com, according to a USPS announcement Wednesday.

Prospective adopters must complete an ID verification process before participating. Letter adoption officially begins Monday, Nov. 16, and gifts must be shipped by Saturday, Dec. 12. The USPS encourages companies and community groups to form teams and adopt entire households together, ensuring families can share in the holiday giving.

Once approved, adopters can browse letters posted on the Operation Santa website, select gifts, and either shop independently or use Santa's Gift Shoppe—powered by Toys"R"Us—which allows direct shipping to recipients. All gifts can be mailed from any participating Post Office location or ordered through the online catalog.

Operation Santa, now in its 114th year, began accepting letters Sept. 14. The program has historically generated thousands of holiday wishes from families and children in need across the country. For more details, visit USPSOperationSanta.com.

item.title: Election 2026: Recount Looms in Escambia Commission Race as Donalds, Moody and Patronis Win
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) — Northwest Florida voters returned several incumbents to office Tuesday, approved local sales-tax measures by wide margins and helped provide strong Panhandle support for Republicans who won Florida's marquee statewide races. But one Escambia County contest remains far from settled. Republican Escambia County…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) — Northwest Florida voters returned several incumbents to office Tuesday, approved local sales-tax measures by wide margins and helped provide strong Panhandle support for Republicans who won Florida's marquee statewide races.

But one Escambia County contest remains far from settled.


Republican Escambia County Commissioner Ashlee Hofberger leads no-party candidate Joe Vinson by just 11 votes in the District 4 race, according to unofficial election-night results.

Hofberger received 12,947 votes, or 50.02%, while Vinson received 12,936, or 49.98%.

The race is headed toward an automatic machine recount because the margin is well below Florida's one-half of one percent recount threshold.


If the margin remains at or below one-quarter of one percent following the machine recount, a manual recount of overvotes and undervotes would follow.

Hofberger told NewsRadio 92.3 Wednesday morning that she's waiting for the process to play out.

“I am eagerly awaiting the rest of the votes to be counted. And I know with the process of the recount, it's going to be a few days, so I am just hoping for patience from the community.”

Florida's first unofficial county returns are due Saturday. Any required machine recount results are due Nov. 12, with official county returns due Nov. 16.


Escambia County results

Elsewhere on the Escambia County Commission, Republican incumbent Mike Kohler won a second term in District 2, receiving 56.32% against Democrat Mathious Robinson.


Two contested Pensacola City Council races also produced winners.


Former council member Sherri Myers defeated District 2 incumbent Charles Bare, 54.39% to 45.61%.


In District 4, Boyce White defeated Brian Cole, 51.55% to 48.45%.


Republican Michelle Salzman won another term in Florida House District 1, while Republican Jon Fay won House District 2.


Escambia County voters also overwhelmingly renewed the county's one-cent Local Option Sales Tax for another decade.


Updated unofficial results show 84,178 votes — 74.96% — in favor and 28,123 — 25.04% — opposed.


The tax has been in place since 1992 and funds capital projects including roads, drainage and stormwater improvements, fire stations, public-safety vehicles, parks and other infrastructure.


Escambia County reported turnout of about 56%, up from roughly 52% during the 2022 midterm election.


Santa Rosa County results


In Santa Rosa County, Marie Locklin won reelection to School Board District 5, receiving 52.48% against Jill Broxson Teston's 47.52%.


Heather Lindsay won another term as Milton mayor with 67.27% of the vote over Howard Steele.


Makayla Charles won Milton City Council Ward 4, Seat 1, while Randy Hebert won Gulf Breeze City Council Seat D.


Jason Rocco won Holley Navarre Fire District Seat 3, and William “Bill” Heineken won Navarre Beach Fire Rescue District Seat 5.


Santa Rosa voters also overwhelmingly approved two sales-tax measures.


The county half-cent surtax received about 73% support.


The Santa Rosa County School District's half-cent sales-tax renewal received about 67%.

Santa Rosa reported voter turnout of 51.43%.


Donalds elected governor

Republican Byron Donalds won Florida's race for governor, defeating Democrat David Jolly in a much closer statewide contest than the results seen in Northwest Florida.

Current unofficial state results show Donalds with 4,131,777 votes — 50.02%.

Jolly received 4,023,425 — 48.71%.


Donalds won Escambia County with about 54% and Santa Rosa County with more than 70%.

He will succeed term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis and become Florida's first Black governor.


Moody wins U.S. Senate race

Republican Ashley Moody won the U.S. Senate special election, allowing her to remain in the seat to which DeSantis appointed her following Marco Rubio's departure to become Secretary of State.


Updated unofficial state results show Moody with about 51% of the vote, compared with roughly 48% for Democratic state Representative Angie Nixon.


Moody's margins were significantly larger locally. She received about 54% in Escambia County and more than 71% in Santa Rosa County.


The election determines who serves the remaining two years of Rubio's Senate term.


Patronis wins full term in Congress

Republican Congressman Jimmy Patronis won a full term representing Florida's 1st Congressional District.


Updated unofficial results show Patronis with 181,723 votes — 62.56%.


Democrat Gay Valimont received 103,429 votes — 35.61% — while no-party candidate Tyler Davis received 5,322.


Patronis first won the seat during a special election in April 2025 following former Congressman Matt Gaetz's resignation.


Republicans win Florida Cabinet races

Republicans also won Florida's three other statewide elected offices.


James Uthmeier defeated Democrat Jose Javier Rodriguez for Attorney General.


Blaise Ingoglia defeated Democrat Annette Taddeo for Chief Financial Officer.


Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson won another term over Democrat Joey Mendoza Atkins.


Each of those races was considerably closer statewide than the results in Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.


Amendment 3 passes; Amendments 1 and 2 fail

Florida voters approved Amendment 3, while rejecting Amendments 1 and 2.

Amendment 3 — dealing with the homestead exemption, assessments of non-homestead property and state spending restrictions — received about 62% statewide support, clearing the 60% required to amend Florida's constitution.


Northwest Florida supported it by larger margins.


Amendment 3 received 66% support in Escambia County and more than 73% in Santa Rosa County.


Amendment 1 failed, receiving about 40% statewide.


Amendment 2 also failed despite receiving a majority of votes. The agricultural property-tax measure received roughly 58% support — short of the 60% constitutional threshold.


Results remain unofficial

Election-night numbers are not Florida's final certified totals.


Counties still have provisional ballots, ballot cures and certain overseas ballots to process.

The first set of unofficial returns is due Saturday. Official county returns are due Nov. 16, and Florida's Elections Canvassing Commission is scheduled to certify statewide results Nov. 17.

The closest local contest remains Escambia County Commission District 4, where only 11 votes currently separate Hofberger and Vinson.


NewsRadio 92.3 will continue following the recount and update the results as additional ballots are processed and the canvassing process continues.

item.title: Florida Republicans Keep Cabinet Control After Election Day Results
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida voters have elected three Republican candidates to statewide cabinet positions, maintaining GOP control of the state's executive offices heading into the next governor's term. According to North Escambia reporting, Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson, Attorney General James Uthmeier, and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia all won…
item.content:encoded:
Florida voters have elected three Republican candidates to statewide cabinet positions, maintaining GOP control of the state's executive offices heading into the next governor's term. According to North Escambia reporting, Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson, Attorney General James Uthmeier, and Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia all won their races on Tuesday.

Uthmeier and Ingoglia were appointed to their current positions by outgoing Gov. Ron DeSantis in 2025, and their election victories mean the incoming governor will largely inherit the sitting cabinet rather than inherit a slate of new appointees.

item.content:encoded: Republican Mike Kohler secured reelection to the Escambia County Commission in District 2 on Tuesday, defeating Democratic challenger Mathious D. Robinson. Kohler took 56.32% of the vote with 9,989 ballots cast in his favor, while Robinson garnered 43.35% with 7,668 votes. Davis in the general election. Patronis garnered 181,723 votes, or 62.56% of the total, according to election results. Valimont received 103,429 votes…
item.content:encoded:
Republican incumbent Jimmy Patronis secured a full term representing Florida's 1st Congressional District on Tuesday, defeating Democratic challenger Gay Valimont and nonpartisan candidate Tyler L. Davis in the general election.

Patronis garnered 181,723 votes, or 62.56% of the total, according to election results. Valimont received 103,429 votes (35.61%), while Davis finished with 5,322 votes (1.83%).

The race marked a rematch between Patronis and Valimont. Patronis has represented the district since a special election and now moves forward with a full two-year term in the House.

item.title: Rep. Salzman wins fourth term in House District 1
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Incumbent Republican Michelle Salzman has won reelection to the Florida House of Representatives, defeating Democratic challenger Francesca Yabraian in District 1 on Tuesday. The seat represents North Escambia County and surrounding areas. With her victory, Salzman will head into her fourth consecutive term representing the district. Following the…
item.content:encoded:
Incumbent Republican Michelle Salzman has won reelection to the Florida House of Representatives, defeating Democratic challenger Francesca Yabraian in District 1 on Tuesday. The seat represents North Escambia County and surrounding areas.

With her victory, Salzman will head into her fourth consecutive term representing the district. Following the passage of Amendment 3 — a constitutional amendment that reduces property tax revenue — Salzman said the Legislature will need to balance revenue losses against the cost of maintaining essential government services in the coming session.

The amendment, approved by Florida voters this week, eliminates the Save Our Homes provision and reduces the assessed value cap on homesteaded properties. Salzman indicated property tax reform will be a key focus as lawmakers work to understand how the change affects state and local budgets.

item.title: Florida voters approve major property tax cut; Amendment 3 passes with 62%
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida residents voted Tuesday to approve Amendment 3, a significant property tax reduction that will nearly quintuple the homestead exemption over the next two years. The measure passed with 62% support, exceeding the 60% threshold required for constitutional amendments. Under the new law, the homestead property tax exemption will jump from the…
item.content:encoded:
Florida residents voted Tuesday to approve Amendment 3, a significant property tax reduction that will nearly quintuple the homestead exemption over the next two years. The measure passed with 62% support, exceeding the 60% threshold required for constitutional amendments.

Under the new law, the homestead property tax exemption will jump from the current $50,000 to $150,000 beginning in 2027, then climb again to $250,000 in 2028. The exemption shields a portion of a home's assessed value from property taxation, effectively lowering tax bills for homeowners who qualify.

Amendment 3 was one of several measures on Tuesday's ballot. While voters embraced the tax cut, they rejected two other proposed amendments, according to reporting on the election results.

The property tax exemption increase is expected to have broad impact across Florida, including in Escambia County and the surrounding region, where homeowners will see relief on their annual property tax obligations once the changes take effect next year.

With nearly 26,000 votes cast in the race, the razor-thin margin triggered Florida's automatic…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Commission District 4 race is headed to an automatic recount after election night results showed incumbent Republican Ashlee Hofberger with an 11-vote lead over nonpartisan challenger Joe Vinson, according to North Escambia reporting.

With nearly 26,000 votes cast in the race, the razor-thin margin triggered Florida's automatic recount provision. The recount will determine whether Hofberger retains her commission seat or if Vinson can overcome the narrow deficit.

item.title: Escambia County Voters Approve 10-Year Sales Tax Renewal
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County residents voted decisively Tuesday to renew the Local Option Sales Tax for another decade, with preliminary results showing 74.96% support for the measure. According to unofficial election results, 84,178 voters backed the renewal while 28,123 opposed it. The LOST generates revenue for county operations and has been a key funding…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County residents voted decisively Tuesday to renew the Local Option Sales Tax for another decade, with preliminary results showing 74.96% support for the measure.

According to unofficial election results, 84,178 voters backed the renewal while 28,123 opposed it. The LOST generates revenue for county operations and has been a key funding source for services and infrastructure projects across Escambia County.

The overwhelming margin of approval gives county commissioners a clear mandate to continue the sales tax, which will remain in effect through 2036. County officials are expected to outline spending priorities and budget impacts once results are certified.

item.title: Florida House Democrats Break GOP Supermajority in Tuesday Election
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida House Democrats achieved a significant political upset in Tuesday's election, breaking the Republican supermajority that has controlled the state legislature for years. The victory means Republicans can no longer act unilaterally on major decisions in Tallahassee, including overriding a governor's veto or bypassing legislative rules…
item.content:encoded:
Florida House Democrats achieved a significant political upset in Tuesday's election, breaking the Republican supermajority that has controlled the state legislature for years. The victory means Republicans can no longer act unilaterally on major decisions in Tallahassee, including overriding a governor's veto or bypassing legislative rules requiring a two-thirds vote — those actions will now require bipartisan support.

Democratic-backed candidates flipped Republican-held districts across South Florida, Central Florida, and the Tampa Bay region, according to a statement from the Florida House Democratic Campaign Committee. Among the victories: Lucia Baez-Geller defeated Republican Rep. Fabian Basabe in Miami-Dade County (a seat where Basabe had been found liable for sexual harassment and battery in a civil case); Michael Ferguson ended nearly 50 years of Republican control of a coastal Broward House seat; and Nikolas Dean flipped a Seminole County district that Republicans had won with just 50.4% of the vote in 2024.

Christine Hunschofsky, the incoming Florida House Democratic leader, called the results a mandate for change. "After years of Republican supermajority control, Floridians across the state stepped up to demand a different direction," she said. Democrats also successfully defended several seats they had narrowly won in 2024, including Leonard Spencer's Orange County district, which he had flipped by just 1,626 votes two years ago.

The shift in the Florida House balance of power marks the first time in years that major legislative decisions will require support from both parties rather than Republicans acting alone.
